A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same title, authors, principal algorithms, and research problem. All pages, including Appendices A–E, are readable; text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, and pseudocode.

before.justification: V3 reports theoretical algorithms, bounds, proofs, and illustrative constructions. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: V4 remains theoretical throughout, including its expanded appendices. Its additional results are mathematical guarantees and impossibility results, not experiments or simulations.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same Hedge updates, mentor-query rules, many-action reduction, and bucket-splitting procedure. Proposition E.2 generalizes the existing query-capping argument from v3's Corollary 5.2.1. The expanded payoff assumptions and additive guarantees extend the analysis without introducing a new learning component.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. V4's additional mathematical scenarios are theoretical constructions, not newly evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. V4's added discussion of constrained MDP algorithms changes related-work positioning, not an evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to allowable payoff functions and query guarantees concern the mathematical model rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. The added impossibility construction in Theorem E.3 is a theoretical result.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical estimation practices. Expectations and concentration inequalities are used in theoretical proofs.

E6.justification: There are no empirical numerical results or qualitative evaluation findings in either version. Added regret bounds and impossibility statements are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 3 extends fixed payoffs to adaptive, time-varying payoffs and changes the query requirement to an expectation. V4 explicitly establishes additive guarantees in Theorem 5.3, Corollary C.1.1, and Appendix D, building on existing intermediate bounds. Proposition E.2 generalizes v3's query-cap result, and new Theorem E.3 addresses impossibility without local generalization even for interval policies and uniform inputs. Appendix A replaces random query counts with deterministic bounds, and Lemma D.3 receives a different proof. The new E.3 proof contains an inequality-direction error.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central catastrophe-avoidance and learnability claims. Section 1.4 adds subconstant additive regret and the associated factor-of-T comparison with conventional regret guarantees as an additional contribution. The threshold-policy result loses its introductory spotlight but remains in Appendix D.

C2.justification: V4 substantively revises the interpretation of the guarantees: Section 3 explains that vanishing regret can be trivial when the mentor eventually fails, while convergence rates still provide information. It emphasizes feature-embedding flexibility and strengthens discussion of why generalization assumptions are needed. Conversely, it removes v3's detailed local-generalization/Lipschitz comparison and incorrectly states the reverse implication in Section 3, contradicting the retained Proposition E.1.

D1.justification: Both versions provide essentially the same algorithm pseudocode, parameter choices, and computational-complexity discussion. Neither supplies experimental implementation details, hardware measurements, or code/data access information that changes between versions.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through a new constrained-MDP discussion, including explicit assumption comparisons with Liu et al. (2021) and Stradi et al. (2024). It replaces the Nash-welfare discussion with more direct multiplicative-online-learning positioning, adds imitation-learning and knowledge-transfer references, and newly asserts the absence of comparable prior negative results. These exceed citation-format changes.

P1.justification: V4 changes states/s to inputs/x, revises associated notation, switches to author-year citations, and edits several explanatory paragraphs. It removes the acknowledgements and introductory paper roadmap. The overall section sequence, appendix organization, and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3's three-panel Figure 2 comparing local generalization with Lipschitz continuity is removed. Its Figure 3 construction survives as v4's Figure 2 with renamed variables. Figure 1 receives a shorter caption, Section 3 gains an annotated equation, and pseudocode and references reflow within the retained single-column layout.

improvement.justification: V4 improves explanation of mentor-quality limitations, expands relevant research comparisons, and explicitly develops additive guarantees. However, v3's correct Lipschitz implication is replaced by an incorrect statement in Section 3, despite Proposition E.1 remaining correct. The new necessity proof in Theorem E.3 also uses an upper bound where its subsequent conclusion requires a lower bound. These errors undermine important explanatory and theoretical additions, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
